title: Establish tiered conversational SLOs, burn-rate escalation, and phased rollout gates for multi-model routing
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Define clear, testable SLOs and a corresponding rollout gate policy for the multi-model routing feature used by conversational chat endpoints. This ticket captures latency bands, uptime objectives, error-budget accounting, burn-rate thresholds for canary progression, and automated fallback triggers when SLOs degrade.

Context: Multi-model routing allows the platform to route requests to different model variants (e.g., full-precision large model, quantized medium model, small low-cost model) based on policy (latency budget, cost, tenant tier). We need production-grade SLO definitions and rollout gates so we can safely roll this feature to hosted and dedicated customers without unexpected regressions to latency/availability or silent quality degradations.

Goals:
- Specify per-workload SLOs (interactive chat streaming and non-streaming) for p50/p95/p99 token-latency and first-token latency and a global availability target.
- Define error budget accounting method (errors + SLO misses) and burn-rate thresholds that map to rollout gate actions (pause, rollback, degrade to fallback routing).
- Provide concrete PromQL (or equivalent) queries and dashboard widgets to measure SLOs and track burn rate in real time.
- Specify rollout sequence and gating windows for canary sizes, metric windows, and escalation steps for hosted and Dedicated customers.
- Establish acceptance criteria, test cases, and runbook links for automated gating in Redwood Console.

Definitions and proposed targets: (proposed baseline for interactive chat workloads)
- First-byte (first-token) latency SLO: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms.
- Per-token streaming latency (per emitted token) SLO: p50 < 15ms, p95 < 45ms, p99 < 130ms.
- End-to-end response latency (non-streaming): p50 < 300ms, p95 < 900ms, p99 < 2000ms.
- Availability SLO: 99.95% (monthly).
- Error definition: 5xx responses, timeouts, truncated responses where token stream ends prematurely.

Error budget accounting:
- Monthly error budget = (1 - availability_slo) * total_minutes_in_month. Example: for 99.95% ≈ 0.05% of time.
- We also count SLO latency window misses as partial budget consumption using severity weights: p99 misses consume 1.0, p95 misses consume 0.25, p50 misses consume 0.05 (weighted by request volume).
- Total budget depletion = weighted_latency_misses + error_count equivalent minutes.

Burn-rate thresholds and automated actions:
- Burn rate < 1x: proceed.
- Burn rate 1x - 3x for 30min: hold canary expansion and notify oncall.
- Burn rate 3x - 6x for 15min: autoscale additional capacity to isolate if possible; if no capacity improvement, pause rollout and shift 25% of canary traffic to fallback model variant.
- Burn rate > 6x for 10min or sustained p99 degradation > 2x baseline: trigger automated rollback to previous routing policy and page SRE.

Rollout gating windows and sizes (canary progression):
- Canary stage 1: 1% traffic for 30 minutes; require burn rate < 1x and p95 < proposed target.
- Canary stage 2: 5% traffic for 60 minutes; require burn rate < 1.5x and p95 within 1.2x of target.
- Canary stage 3: 20% traffic for 2 hours; require burn rate < 2x and p99 within 1.5x of target.
- Full rollout: 100% after successful stage 3 and CR review.
- For Dedicated/private customers: start at 0.5% tenant sample and require longer observation windows (2x duration) before progressing.

Fallback and graceful degradation policy:
- If gating triggers pause/rollback, immediately switch affected traffic to the next compatible model variant (e.g., quantized medium model) and enable prefix KV cache bypass if cache contamination suspected.
- Maintain a maximum degradation cap: maximum allowed increase in median latency during fallback is 2x baseline unless explicitly approved by PM.

Monitoring queries & dashboards (examples to implement):
- PromQL p99 first-token latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_first_token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,model,region))
- Burn-rate: (errors + weighted_latency_misses) / theoretical_budget_per_minute
- Dashboard panels: per-region/per-model latency envelopes, burn-rate heatmap by tenant tier, canary traffic distribution and recent auto-actions.

Notes and trade-offs:
- Targets above are intentionally conservative for p99 to reduce risk during rollout; final numbers may be tuned based on aggregated latency distributions across top 20% tenants.
- Weighted miss accounting allows teams to avoid being dominated by transient p50 jitter while still prioritizing tail behavior.
- Rollout windows balance speed and safety; Dedicated customers get slower, more conservative progression to respect isolation and change management needs.

Next steps:
- PM to align with SRE on burn-rate math and alert routing by 2026-02-22.
- ENG to prototype PromQL queries and dashboard panels (ENG-40988).
- Observability to add dashboard and produce sample alerts (Jenna Li).
- Schedule gated canary for hosted in runtime-2.4 release and include Dedicated pilot list.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation exposes the SLO metrics (first-token, per-token streaming, end-to-end) for every model variant and region in Grafana/Datasource.
Console can initiate canary stages with configured windows and automatically execute pause/rollback/fallback actions when burn-rate thresholds are crossed.
Alerts and oncall runbooks created for each burn-rate threshold and mapped to SRE rotation.
Automated integration tests validate canary traffic percentages and simulated burn-rate scenarios in CI with synthetic load.
Dedicated customer pilot list exists and pilot rollout plan is documented with longer windows and approval steps.
steps_to_validate: Deploy canary to internal staging with synthetic traffic generator that produces controlled latency and error patterns.
Simulate progressive burn-rate scenarios (1x, 3x, 6x) and assert Console executes configured actions (hold, partial-fallback, rollback).
Run e2e test that verifies fallback route returns valid responses and that degradation cap is honored.
Verify dashboards show correct weighted-latency-miss accounting and that monthly error budget math matches example calculation.
Run pre-release demo with SRE, runtime, and Observability; gather sign-off.
notes: Avoid hardcoding model names in rollout gates—use compatible_model_label to keep routing policies portable.
Consider adding per-tenant safety locks (manual approval) for top 5% revenue tenants.
Security review required due to dedicated/private behavioural differences in routing and potential telemetry exposure.
